question: Does the slice burst need NMDAR activity? (readout control)
compound_action: d-AP5 (50 uM as used by the source); competitive glutamate-site NMDAR antagonist, tool compound
system: Synapsin-Cre Wwox neuron-deleted neocortical slices, layer II/III, P13-P17, mouse
wwox_evidence: Observed: bursts in 36 of 42 knockout slices vanish with d-AP5 (51 bursts, 5 slices, 3 animals; Breton 2021). Not observed: that the NMDAR current is raised.
external_precedent: Rat oocyte functional Ki, GluN2A 390 vs GluN2B 2,800 nM (7.2x) in one document and 280 vs 460 nM (1.6x) in another: no strong subunit preference.
pharmacology: Subunit values graded; no compound-specific value in the WWOX preparation.
pharmacology_limits: Oocyte values are not slice values; a surmountable block; the catalogue gives no potency in a WWOX preparation.
counter_evidence: Cannot separate raised gain from permissive necessity; wild-type matched-trigger slices may lose bursts equally (then the block is generic).
next_experiment: Run as the last step in every slice (positive control and ceiling).

question: Which share of the slice NMDAR current is carried by GluN2B-containing receptors, and do bursts follow it?
compound_action: GluN2B negative allosteric modulators at the ifenprodil site: ifenprodil and Ro 25-6981 as tools, radiprodil as clinical-stage comparator
system: Same slice preparation; potencies from human or rat recombinant receptors in oocytes
wwox_evidence: Bursts are d-APV-sensitive; NMDAR current not measured (so the GluN2B share f at this age is unknown).
external_precedent: Two independent papers compiled in one review: ifenprodil 110 vs 39,500 nM (359x, human, 3 uM glycine, -40 mV) and Ro 25-6981 9 vs 52,000 nM (5,778x, rat context); one source for the mouse layer II/III ifenprodil sensitivity exists at abstract level only.
pharmacology: GluN2B over GluN2A by about 70-fold (eliprodil) to 360-fold (ifenprodil) and 5,800-fold (Ro 25-6981) across tools and conditions; the stated reduction of the isolated current is an UPPER BOUND, sum of f_i x Emax_i x occupancy_i.
pharmacology_limits: Ifenprodil inhibition is incomplete and triheteromers are partly inhibited; conditions differ between the two compounds; radiprodil has only complex-level values (not determinable).
counter_evidence: A steeper-than-linear burst fall is not a valid discriminator alone (burst generation is threshold-like).
next_experiment: Measure f with a saturating GluN2B NAM; then titrate the NAM, an equal-current d-AP5 and a low-trapping pore blocker, with a GluN2A NAM and two unrelated GluN2B NAMs as controls.

question: Is subunit selectivity needed at all to reduce NMDAR-dependent bursting?
compound_action: Pore blockers: memantine, ketamine (esketamine separate), dizocilpine
system: Recombinant receptors in U2OS, CHO and HEK293 cells (flux), oocytes elsewhere
wwox_evidence: No result of these compounds in a WWOX system; the class is carded as an NMDAR intervention class.
external_precedent: Approved in adults for other uses; ChEMBL labels the generic NMDA-receptor group with 'negative allosteric modulator' on the salt records, which means non-competitive and not subunit- or site-resolved.
pharmacology: GluN2A-versus-GluN2B ratios of 4x or less; no subunit selectivity detected.
pharmacology_limits: Flux formats have no holding voltage (the controlling variable for use-dependent blockers); one arm spans 30-fold.
counter_evidence: Direction of the small ratios is not resolved between documents.
next_experiment: Use as the subunit-indifferent comparator at matched fractional current.

question: If NMDAR gain were limiting, would an opposed action worsen bursting?
compound_action: Co-agonist or positive-modulator direction: dalzanemdor (SAGE-718), D-cycloserine, glycine; GluN2A NAM TCN-201 as a subunit-assignment control
wwox_evidence: None; excitatory-gain readings are one of several live rivals.
external_precedent: Dalzanemdor EC50 79 vs 86 nM (GluN2B vs GluN2A; one origin, Hill 2022).
pharmacology_limits: Reference values from one system; not transferred to the slice.
counter_evidence: If bursts do not increase, permissive necessity is favoured over raised gain.
next_experiment: Apply a positive modulator to heterozygous and wild-type slices and score bursts.

question: Does raising ambient GABA offset the inhibitory deficit?
system: Human infants (case reports); no WWOX slice or mouse arm
wwox_evidence: Case reports of WWOX-related epilepsy: 2 benefit, 3 null, 1 partial, 1 unresolved (queried, not read in full).
external_precedent: Labelled for infantile spasms and refractory partial seizures; boxed warning for visual field loss.
pharmacology: Time-dependent inactivation constant only; no brain potency stated.
pharmacology_limits: Not testable in acute slice; spasms are a different seizure type from slice bursts.
counter_evidence: Cannot be read as a test of the phasic IPSC deficit.
next_experiment: Tonic holding current and phasic IPSC charge in the same cells; a chronic mouse arm would be needed.

question: Does a benzodiazepine-site potentiator compensate the lost fast GABA-A inhibition during exposure?
compound_action: Clobazam and N-desmethylclobazam (benzodiazepine-site positive modulators); zolpidem and clonazepam to attribute the subunit
wwox_evidence: sIPSC amplitude 57.3 to 27.5 pA (about -52 percent; KCl internal solution, pooled events); heterozygote against wild type not reported.
external_precedent: Subtype data in three primary papers; selectivity disputed. Potentiation of a few-fold at low GABA in recombinant receptors.
pharmacology: Emax 100 to 317 percent at EC10 (rat HEK293) and 203 to 270 percent at EC20 (human oocytes); conditions differ.
pharmacology_limits: Restoration of a roughly halved amplitude to control is not guaranteed; locus of the loss unmeasured (it changes interpretation, not whether the arm can be run).
counter_evidence: Burst reduction equal in wild-type matched-trigger slices would show network state, not knockout specificity.
next_experiment: Same-cell triad (with miniature IPSCs in TTX), then graded potentiator with measured IPSC charge.

question: Is the inhibitory loss release- or clearance-limited rather than receptor-limited?
external_precedent: GAT1 IC50 70 nM (human) against micromolar GAT2, GAT3 and BGT-1 (mixed species).
pharmacology: Human GAT1 potency from the catalogue.
counter_evidence: No effect on bursts despite a longer IPSC decay, or a paradoxical increase, would weaken it.
next_experiment: IPSC decay and tonic current against burst frequency, at matched IPSC charge with the previous case.

question: Is an intrinsic depolarisation (Kv7) sufficient to explain bursting? (counter-hypothesis)
compound_action: Ezogabine (retigabine), Kv7 opener, reversed by XE991
wwox_evidence: Resting potential -79.25 / -75.51 / -73.62 mV (wild type / heterozygote / knockout); input resistance shared by heterozygote and knockout.
external_precedent: A serious adverse-event history is recorded for the compound (not verified here); another Kv7 opener is in late clinical development (one assay, not transferred).
pharmacology: Exact EC50 values span 350 to 4,210 nM for Kv7.2 (12-fold) and 430 to 11,200 nM for Kv7.2/7.3 (26-fold) across ChEMBL documents; Kv7.2 homomer 930 against Kv7.2/7.3 heteromer 1,720 nM in one document is a limited comparison.
counter_evidence: If Vm-matched wild-type slices burst while the opener stops knockout bursts, the intrinsic reading is weakened.
next_experiment: Opener titrated to the 5.6 mV shift, with Vm-matched wild-type slices.

question: Does lithium act through GSK3 de-repression in WWOX loss?
compound_action: Lithium (the activity sits on the Li+ ion record; salts carry none); ion- and Mg2+-competitive at GSK3, second curated target IMPase
system: Wwox-null preweaning mouse, provoked-seizure scoring (whole animal)
wwox_evidence: Seizure severity after a provoking injection fell in all three genotypes including wild type: the functional measure exists and is non-specific. pSer9 of GSK3beta is lower in the null brain on a single blot (one lane per genotype per region, no statistics).
external_precedent: Approved for other indications; narrow therapeutic index.
pharmacology: About 2 mM, two review-sourced rows flagged outside the typical range.
pharmacology_limits: Primary origin of the figure not established; GtoPdb value not re-verified.
counter_evidence: Many other lithium actions; Wnt direction possibly adverse.
next_experiment: Kinase-activity or substrate-phosphorylation readout in a Wwox-null system with a differently acting GSK3 inhibitor.

question: Does GSK3 kinase activity, not only pSer9, change in WWOX loss, and in which direction does each inhibitor class move the Wnt readout?
compound_action: Tool experiment: an ATP-site inhibitor (LY-2090314), lithium, tideglusib (irreversible, non-ATP-competitive) and an Axin-pathway control that itself needs GSK3
system: Wwox-null cells or tissue; human knockout organoids for the Wnt readout
wwox_evidence: pSer9 decreased with total GSK3beta unchanged (single blot); Axin-like docking motif at WWOX 388-407; Wnt target genes up in knockout organoids (confounded by maturity).
external_precedent: Tau Ser396 down and beta-catenin up under a GSK3beta inhibitor in SH-SY5Y (one document, qualitative, not WWOX).
pharmacology: GSK3A/GSK3B ratio about 1 for the named compounds; 86 same-document pairs above 10-fold exist for other compounds; tideglusib potency spans 5 nM to above 10 uM with a 12.8-fold shift on 3 h pre-incubation.
pharmacology_limits: No isoform lever for the named compounds; wild-type pair 1.67; GtoPdb figures not re-verified.
counter_evidence: Wnt signalling does not use Ser9, so the pSer9 versus Wnt conflict is weaker than first stated.
next_experiment: Measure kinase activity and Tau pS396/S404 with beta-catenin phospho and AXIN2/LEF1 in Wwox-null cells, comparing the classes.
